note: Sample ledger shipped with the documentation site. Illustrative data for the dashboard — not the output of a real nightly run.

nights.hypothesis: Raising the flywheel promotion gate's minimum holdout size from n=40 to n=60 removes false ACCEPTs without costing true lift.
nights.finding: n=60 eliminated 2 of the 3 historical false promotions while keeping every true lift. The gate got stricter without getting blinder.
nights.evidence: Replayed all 9 archived promotions: false positives 3/9 → 1/9; true-lift recall held at 6/6. Replay receipts verified against stored flywheel state.

nights.hypothesis: Routing tier-1 transforms through the WASM booster before the LLM tier cuts median hook latency by more than 30%.
nights.finding: Median latency moved 8% — inside run-to-run noise. The booster path was already taken on 91% of tier-1 calls, so there was almost nothing left to reroute.
nights.evidence: n=240 hook invocations. Median 512 ms → 471 ms; paired bootstrap 95% CI [-14%, +2%] crosses zero. Pre-existing booster hit rate measured at 91%.

nights.hypothesis: A genome that biases the generator toward edit-by-midpoint transfers from the training verticals to the held-out ones.
nights.finding: No measurement was taken. The baseline built cleanly and the candidate genome compiled, but every scoring call was refused for lack of credentials — so the hypothesis carries over untested rather than answered.
nights.evidence: LLM_EVAL=blocked — 0 model calls completed (no provider key in the session). Build green, control-plane probes green, baseline artifacts retained for tomorrow.

nights.hypothesis: At a fixed token budget, 3 Darwin generations of 8 candidates beats 6 generations of 4.
nights.finding: Wider-and-shallower won. The extra population per generation mattered more than the extra generations, at equal spend.
nights.evidence: 60-task holdout, n=60. Score 0.612 → 0.647; paired bootstrap p=0.021. Token spend within 2% between arms. Reward-hack scan clean.

nights.hypothesis: A second adversarial critic pass surfaces reward-hack surface the first pass misses.
nights.finding: The second pass found nothing the first had not already flagged, across 40 candidate diffs, and roughly doubled critique cost. One pass is the right number.
nights.evidence: 40 candidate diffs, two-pass vs one-pass. Additional findings: 0. Critique cost +103%. Agreement between passes: 40/40.

nights.hypothesis: Consolidating near-duplicate memories before indexing improves recall precision without losing coverage.
nights.finding: The budget ceiling was reached partway through the baseline sweep. 22 of 60 tasks were scored — too few to separate the arms, so no claim is made either way.
nights.evidence: HALT: budget at $18.40 against an $18.00 ceiling. 22/60 tasks scored before the halt. Partial baseline retained; the ledger row was written by the halt path.

nights.hypothesis: A normalizer shared across the SQL and math verticals raises extraction agreement without touching either gold set.
nights.finding: Agreement rose substantially and the gold answers were provably untouched — the lift came from the normalizer, not from moving the target.
nights.evidence: Inter-vertical agreement 0.71 → 0.83 over n=180 items, p<0.01. Gold-answer files hash-verified identical before and after. Reward-hack scan clean.

nights.hypothesis: Summarising tool results above 2 KB before they enter context saves tokens without hurting task success.
nights.finding: It saved the tokens and cost the success. A 14% token reduction came with a measurable 4-point drop in task success — a real regression, not noise.
nights.evidence: n=50 tasks. Tokens -14%; success 0.58 → 0.54; paired bootstrap 95% CI [-0.09, -0.01], excludes zero.
